meta.description: Sentence-level AI tells consolidated from anti_patterns.json into matchable entries. Tier-1 enforcement. gate=hard entries are deterministically detected and block prohibitions_clear; gate=checklist entries are surfaced as located must-clear items the LLM must rewrite or justify. Non-uniformity (foundation.enforcement.non_uniformity_scope) does NOT apply to this layer.
meta.usage: Consumed by humanizer_check_text. Not a substitute for the prose guidance in structural_patterns.json.

structures.name: didactic_disclaimer
structures.description: 'It is important to note that...' style preamble that adds no information.

phrases: it is important to note that
it is crucial to remember that

structures.fix: Cut the preamble and state the fact directly.

structures.name: empty_opener
structures.description: Filler openers with no legitimate use.
structures.fix: Cut entirely. Be specific about what is changing and how.

structures.name: participle_tail
structures.description: Comma + present-participle tail that adds interpretation without new information.
structures.fix: Delete the dangling -ing clause, or commit to the interpretation in its own sentence.

structures.name: significance_puffery
structures.description: Inflated framing of mundane facts as sweeping historical claims.

detection.pattern: \b(marking a (pivotal|crucial|defining|key) (moment|chapter)|setting the stage for|part of a broader (movement|trend|effort) to|underscores its enduring (significance|importance))\b

structures.fix: Strip the editorializing and state what actually happened.

structures.name: negative_parallelism
structures.description: 'not just X, but also Y' / 'not only X but Y' contrast inflation.
structures.fix: State the point directly with a simple conjunction.

structures.name: despite_faces_challenges
structures.description: 'Despite its X, [subject] faces challenges...' hedge-praise formula.
structures.fix: Replace with specific problems and specific responses; drop the framing formula.

structures.name: that_clause_subject
structures.description: Sentence opening with a 'That ... is' clausal subject.
structures.fix: Move the evidence/source to the front; let the claim follow.

structures.name: x_not_y_contrastive
structures.description: 'X, not Y' contrastive binary that reads constructed.
structures.fix: Make the positive claim and let it stand, or use a separate sentence for the contrast.

structures.name: stacked_nominalization
structures.description: Three or more 'X of' nominalizations in one sentence.
structures.fix: Unpack the nouns back into verbs; name the agent.

structures.name: this_chain
structures.description: Three or more consecutive sentences opening with This/These/It.
structures.fix: Leave causal links implicit; vary sentence openings.

structures.name: negation_flip_antithesis
structures.description: Two-sentence copula flip: 'X is not Y. It is Z.' The single most characteristic antithesis of LLM prose. A two-sentence relative of BS-006 ('not just X but Y') and BS-011 ('X, not Y'), which the single-sentence checks miss.
structures.fix: Make the positive claim and let it stand. Do not negate an alternative in one sentence and flip to the real point in the next.
structures.research_basis: Named the LLM's single most-favored rhetorical move ('it's not X; it's Y') in the Dead Language Society rhetorical analysis (2025); corroborates proposed-rules #5.

structures.name: rarely_flip_aphorism
structures.description: A disguised antithesis: a copula claim hedged with rarely/seldom/never, then flipped to the 'real' point in a second copula sentence. 'The interesting move is rarely the new automation. It is deciding what to leave alone.'
structures.fix: Drop the 'is rarely X. It is Y' flip; state plainly what the point or the work actually was.

structures.name: wh_cleft_pronouncement
structures.description: A pseudo-cleft fronted by a 'What ...' clause pivoting on a copula into a noun, used for portentous effect: 'What matters here is the design.' Sibling of the that-clause subject (BS-010).
structures.fix: Make the plain claim. Drop the 'What ... is ...' framing and lead with the thing itself.
structures.research_basis: proposed-rules #1; scoped to declaratives (interrogatives end in '?' and do not match).

structures.name: meta_framing_opener
structures.description: Opening a passage by announcing its own thesis abstractly: 'The point of the redesign is ...', 'The key here is ...'. Over-signals structure before showing the concrete thing.
structures.fix: Lead with the concrete thing and let the reader infer the point. Cut the 'The point of X is' scaffolding.
structures.research_basis: proposed-rules #6.

structures.name: disclaimer_reversal
structures.description: A disclaiming sentence ('I won't claim/pretend/promise ...') immediately followed by a short emphatic 'But ...' reversal. Inter-sentential relative of BS-013; the single-sentence antithesis checks miss it.
structures.fix: State what you can stand behind, plainly, in one move. Drop the disclaimer-then-flip rhythm.
structures.research_basis: proposed-rules PR2-#2; in-the-wild audit 2026-06-28.

structures.name: copula_maxim_closer
structures.description: A paragraph or section closes on a short abstract-subject copula maxim ('The craft is mostly restraint.'). Generalizes BS-014 beyond rarely/never aphorisms. Detected heuristically (src/checker/structures.py): paragraph-final, <=10 words, opens with The/My/Our, an abstract subject noun, a copula main verb, no proper noun or number.
structures.fix: End on the concrete thing, not a distilled lesson about it. If the maxim is earned, attach it to a specific action rather than floating it as a closer.
structures.research_basis: proposed-rules PR2-#3; in-the-wild audit 2026-06-28.

structures.name: locative_pseudocleft
structures.description: A pseudo-cleft pivoting on where/when/how rather than 'what' ('The gap between those two facts was where the work got lost.'). Sibling of BS-015. Scoped to an article-led noun-phrase subject so demonstrative/expletive forms ('This is how', 'Here is where', 'That was when') do not trip it.
structures.fix: Lead with the subject doing the thing: 'Work got lost in that gap.' Drop the 'X is where ...' frame.
structures.research_basis: proposed-rules PR2-#5; in-the-wild audit 2026-06-28. Pattern tightened from the proposed bare 'is/was where' to an article-led subject to suppress 'This is how' / 'Here is where' false positives.

structures.name: verb_antithesis_pair
structures.description: Two short sentences repeating a content verb with a polarity flip ('AI carries the busywork. It never carries the judgment.'). Verb-based relative of the copula antithesis BS-013. Detected heuristically (src/checker/structures.py): fires only when the negated verb is actually repeated, by form or stem, from the prior sentence, so ordinary narrative ('It never finished.') does not match.
structures.fix: Make the positive claim once. If the boundary matters, state it without mirroring the verb in the negative.
structures.research_basis: proposed-rules PR2-#6; in-the-wild audit 2026-06-28. Implemented as a verb-repetition heuristic rather than the proposed bare 'It never <verb>' regex to avoid firing on unrelated negations.

structures.name: noun_participle_fragment
structures.description: A verbless 'Noun, past-participle.' sentence: a determiner-led noun phrase, a comma, and a trailing past participle, ending there ('The same board, rebuilt.', 'The homepage, reimagined.'). Past-participle sibling of BS-005 (present-participle tail). Bounded to a sentence-initial determiner with the participle as the final token, so it fires only on the verbless fragment, never on full clauses ('He left the room, defeated.', 'The board, which we rebuilt, is live.').
structures.fix: Give it a subject and a finite verb ('We rebuilt the same board.'), or fold the participle into the neighboring sentence. Drop the noun-comma-participle fragment.
structures.research_basis: In-the-wild reviewer feedback 2026-07-03 on prose that had passed the checker clean: 'The same board, rebuilt.' flagged as the 'Noun, past-participle.' construction. Scoped to a sentence-initial determiner-led NP with the participle as the terminal token to preserve the fragment guarantee and suppress false positives; the [a-z]{3,}ed floor excludes short -ed look-alikes (red/bed/shed), and the missing comma keeps fixed idioms ('Case closed.') quiet.

structures.name: meta_label
structures.description: A standalone meta-label line or heading that names the artifact's own format or length instead of its subject ('In 200 words', 'In brief', 'At a high level', 'To put it simply'). The mechanizable slice of the performative-framing beat: a self-aware flourish that performs concision or structure rather than carrying content. Fires ONLY when the label IS the whole bounded line/sentence (optionally one terminal mark, then a line break or end), so embedded uses ('At a high level, the system does X.') never match. TL;DR is deliberately excluded (common and acceptable in casual writing). The judgment sub-forms, self-satisfied closers, first-person meta-commentary, paradox-substitution headlines, are the self_review 'performative framing beat' rubric item, not this detector.
structures.fix: Replace the format/length/brevity label with a phrase about the content itself, or cut it and let the section's content name it. Do not announce structure; let the structure be the structure.
structures.research_basis: In-the-wild reviewer feedback 2026-07-06 on prose run through the humanizer: meta labels ('in 200 words', 'the reading, in brief') survived as self-aware flourishes. Scoped to a standalone bounded label with a terminal-only trailing guard so the embedding-prone phrases ('at a high level', 'to put it simply') fire only as labels, never mid-sentence. Sibling of the closer detector BS-018; the judgment sub-forms live in the self_review rubric. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-performative-framing-beat-design.md.

structures.name: validation_reassurance
structures.description: Unsolicited second-person reassurance in a fixed frame ('You're not alone.', 'You're not imagining it.', 'You're not broken.', 'It's not just you.'). The single most-cited NEW 2026 AI tell: the model switches into therapeutic validation that reads as bizarre in most content (business posts, docs, marketing). High-precision because it matches only the 'you're not <predicate>' / 'it's not just you' frames, so ordinary negations ('You're not sure yet.', 'You are not authorized.') never match. Legitimate in genuine supportive/empathetic writing, which is why it is checklist (rewrite or justify), never hard.

detection.pattern: \byou(?:['’]re| are) not\s+(?:alone|broken|crazy|failing|imagining|overreacting|weak|the only one)\b|\bit(?:['’]s| is) not just you\b

structures.fix: Cut the reassurance, or replace it with the specific thing you actually want to say. If the piece genuinely calls for empathy, make it concrete rather than a canned 'you're not X' formula.
structures.research_basis: Forbes, 'The 15 New Giveaway Signs Of AI-Generated Content' (2026-02-03): AI switching into unsolicited validation ('You're not imagining it', 'You're not alone', 'You're not broken') flagged as the standout new tell, incongruous in business/productivity content. Frame-scoped to keep false positives near zero.

structures.name: vague_authority_attribution
structures.description: An appeal to an unnamed authority as evidence ('Researchers say...', 'Studies show...', 'Experts agree...', 'It is widely believed...', 'Many argue...'). A content-level AI tell distinct from credibility_insistence (which flags reality-assertion words like real/actual): here the sentence borrows authority it never names. The verb list is scoped to epistemic-claim frames, so a named or specific reference with a concrete action ('The researchers at MIT published their data') does not match. Checklist because attributed uses are legitimate, the fix is to name the source or cut the appeal.
structures.fix: Name who: cite the specific study, person, or body, and link or reference it. If you cannot name a source, drop the claim or state it as your own view.
structures.research_basis: Wikipedia 'Signs of AI writing' (2026): 'vague attributions', attributing claims to undefined authorities ('researchers', 'observers', 'scholarship') without naming them, listed as a core content tell. Scoped to unnamed-agent + epistemic-verb frames so named/specific references pass.

structures.name: question_fragment_cadence
structures.description: The 'The best part? It's this.' rhetorical tic: a sentence-initial determiner-led noun-phrase fragment ending in '?', immediately answered by a short sentence ('The result? A total win.', 'My advice? Take the job.'). Named repeatedly as a 2026 ChatGPT fingerprint (the 'contrasting question with a short answer' pattern). Scoped to a determiner-led NP of up to three words so WH-questions ('What is the best part?') and mid-sentence questions ('Did you see the result?') never match, the determiner must sit at a sentence boundary.
structures.fix: State the point as a declarative sentence. If the setup-and-payoff is earned, use it once; repeated question-fragment beats read as a tic.
structures.research_basis: Walter Writes / PlusAI 'most overused ChatGPT patterns' (2026) and in-the-wild reports: 'contrasting questions with short answers' ('The best part? It's this. The kicker? It's that.') as a durable 2026 structural fingerprint. NP-fragment + boundary scoping keeps genuine questions clear.

structures.name: when_it_comes_to_opener
structures.description: The 'When it comes to X...' sentence opener, a very-high-frequency AI phrase frame that sets up a topic with an empty preamble instead of stating the point. Scoped to a sentence boundary with a trailing comma so mid-sentence uses ('she knew when it comes to a vote') never match.
structures.fix: Cut the preamble and state the point. 'When it comes to pricing, we keep it simple' becomes 'Our pricing is simple.'
structures.research_basis: Bloomberry 'AI Sentence DNA' (2026): 'when it comes to' listed Very High across all models. Boundary plus trailing-comma scoping keeps false positives near zero.

structures.name: world_state_opener
structures.description: The grand temporal/world-state opener ('In a world where...', 'In an era of...', 'In an age where...', 'In a time of...'), a very-high-frequency AI hook that opens on a sweeping generalization. Complements the flagged transition 'In today's rapidly evolving' and BS-016 meta_framing_opener. Scoped to a sentence boundary and a fixed determiner-plus-noun-plus-where/of skeleton so a literal 'in a world of magic' mid-sentence never matches.
structures.fix: Cut the cosmic setup and open on the specific. Say what is changing and for whom.
structures.research_basis: Bloomberry 'AI Sentence DNA' (2026): 'In a world where...' hook formula, Very High across all models. Boundary scoping keeps mid-sentence literal uses clear.

structures.name: pivotal_role_frame
structures.description: The 'plays a [pivotal/crucial/key/central...] role in' template. The evaluative adjectives are individually flagged, but the template slips through when the adjective is an un-flagged option (key/central/major), so the frame itself is matched. Restricted to evaluative adjectives so a neutral 'play a supporting role in the film' does not match.
structures.fix: Say what the thing actually does. 'Monitoring plays a pivotal role in catching problems' becomes 'Monitoring catches problems early.'
structures.research_basis: Bloomberry 'AI Sentence DNA' (2026) and 2026 overused-phrase lists: 'play a pivotal/crucial role in' as a recurring filler template. Adjective allow-list keeps neutral role-descriptions clear.

structures.name: solution_pivot
structures.description: The 'That's where X comes in.' marketing pivot-to-product beat ('This is where we come in.'). Scoped to a sentence-initial 'that's/this is where' plus a terminal 'comes in.' so the idiom 'comes in handy' and ordinary locatives ('this is where we live') never match.
structures.fix: State what the product does directly instead of staging a reveal.
structures.research_basis: Bloomberry 'AI Sentence DNA' (2026): the reveal/solution-pivot cadence. Terminal scoping ('comes in.') keeps 'comes in handy' and locatives clear.

structures.name: empathy_conditional_opener
structures.description: The 'If you've ever struggled with...' empathy opener, a fixed second-person conditional that manufactures relatability, in the same family as BS-023 validation_reassurance. Scoped to a sentence boundary plus 'you've/you have ever' plus an empathy verb (struggled/wondered/felt/...), so anecdotal openers ('If you've ever been to Paris') and mid-sentence uses do not match.
structures.fix: Open on the concrete situation, not a canned 'if you've ever felt X' hook.
structures.research_basis: Bloomberry 'AI Sentence DNA' (2026): empathy opener 'If you've ever struggled with...'. Empathy-verb allow-list plus boundary scoping keeps genuine conditional anecdotes clear.

structures.name: metaphorical_carry
structures.description: Metaphorical 'carry': the fixed abstract collocation ('the design carries the weight', 'carrying the burden of the argument') and the text-unit intransitive ('eight words to carry'). A strong Claude-register tell: the verb performs gravity while no one does anything. FP-guarded by an abstract-object allow-list and, on the intransitive branch, a text-unit head noun, so literal carrying ('too heavy to carry', 'carry the groceries', 'the truck carries the load') never matches. 'load' and 'freight' were dropped from the object list during design because logistics prose uses them literally. Known accepted boundary: the fixed idiom 'carries the weight of the world' does fire; at gate=checklist that is a rewrite-or-justify prompt, and the idiom is a cliche worth a second look either way. Deliberately NOT a bare 'carry' word-flag: 'carry' is a high-frequency ordinary verb and a bare flag is the flow_over_surface_features low-ceiling trap. The wider family (any abstract noun as subject of 'carry') is not mechanizable without a parser and lives in the self_review abstraction-as-agent item.
structures.fix: Name the actual agent and the actual effect. 'The layout carries the weight of the argument' -> 'The layout is what makes the argument land.' For the label form, say what the words must do: 'Eight words to carry' -> 'Eight words, and they have to do the whole job.'
structures.research_basis: In-the-wild report (2026-08-06) plus caveats.json metrics_do_not_apply_to_label_text (2026-08-03), which recorded 'Eight words to carry' as a genuine AI-register tell that the checker missed.

structures.name: honestly_fragment_opener
structures.description: A standalone one-word interrogative opener promising candour and delivering a platitude ('Honestly? Most people don't follow up.'). Scoped to a fixed adverb set as the WHOLE bounded fragment at a sentence or line boundary, so quoted dialogue ('"Honestly?" she said.') and mid-sentence uses never match.
structures.fix: Delete the fragment and state the claim. If the point is not actually candid or contrarian, the opener is advertising something the sentence does not deliver.
structures.research_basis: Forbes, 'The 15 New Giveaway Signs Of AI-Generated Content' (2026-02-03), tell #3: "'Honestly?' followed by nothing honest".

structures.name: quiet_prestige_modifier
structures.description: The 'everything is quietly something' tic: 'quiet confidence', 'quiet rebellion', 'quietly reshaping'. Both branches are allow-listed ('quiet' + an abstract-quality noun, or 'quietly' + a transformation verb), so ordinary use ('a quiet room', 'she quietly closed the door') passes. This is the collocation, not the word: a bare 'quiet' flag was rejected on 2026-07-13 as the flow_over_surface_features trap, and that rejection stands.
structures.fix: Cut the modifier or replace it with the evidence. 'Quiet confidence' -> say what the person did that showed it. 'Quietly reshaping the industry' -> name the change and who noticed.
structures.research_basis: Forbes (2026-02-03), tell #5: 'Everything is quietly something', 'quiet confidence', 'quiet rebellion', 'quietly growing', 'the quiet truth'.

structures.name: concessive_balance_hedge
structures.description: The risk-averse both-sides frame that concludes nothing: 'While X has benefits, it also carries risks.' Scoped so BOTH the hedge verb and its object are allow-listed, leaving ordinary concessive 'While' clauses clear. Distinct frame from BS-007 ('despite ... faces ... challenges').
structures.fix: Pick the claim you actually want to make and make it. If the trade-off is real, name the specific cost and who pays it, rather than balancing the sentence for its own sake.
structures.research_basis: Gibson, 'The Predictable Rhetoric of AI-Generated Text' (Medium, 2026-04), device #3 'Balancing Hedging'; corroborated by Forbes tell #13 'faux balance without consequence'.

structures.name: internal_cross_reference
structures.description: Over-tidy self-reference: 'As mentioned above', 'As we discussed earlier', 'As noted previously'. Legitimate in long technical and academic documents, which is why it is checklist (rewrite or justify), never hard.
structures.fix: Cut it and restate the point in three words, or trust the reader to remember. Keep it only where a real document needs a genuine back-reference.
structures.research_basis: Forbes (2026-02-03), tell #14: 'internal references that are too tidy'.

structures.name: deepening_invitation
structures.description: The therapeutic prompt to go deeper: 'Let that sink in.', 'Do you want to sit with that for a while?', 'Are you ready to go deeper?', 'Read that again.' A fixed phrase set rather than a productive frame, so precision is near-total. Family relative of BS-023 (validation_reassurance).
structures.fix: Delete it. If the point deserves weight, give it weight with a fact or a consequence, not an instruction to feel something.
structures.research_basis: Forbes (2026-02-03), tell #7: 'questions designed to deepen', 'Do you want to sit with that for a while?', 'Are you ready to go deeper?'

structures.name: withheld_insight_teaser
structures.description: The setup that announces a payoff it rarely delivers: 'Here's the kicker', 'the part most people miss', 'what nobody tells you'. Scoped to the 'most people|nobody|no one' + 'miss|get wrong|tell you|know' skeleton plus the fixed 'here's the kicker'. Adjacent to 'Here's the thing', which was rejected on 2026-07-25 as register-dependent; that rejection stands; what is flagged here is the marker PLUS the withheld-insight claim.
structures.fix: Lead with the insight itself. If it is genuinely counterintuitive the reader will notice without being told to.
structures.research_basis: Forbes (2026-02-03), tells #1 'announcing the good part' ('Here's the kicker') and #4 'setup phrases that don't deliver' ('Here's the part most people miss').
